rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer blocks point, don't restate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All maintainer content (failure modes L15, §6 carve-out L17, prompt-block anchoring L19, open item L21-22, cut note L24) is unique to this file's own design decisions; nothing restates a cross-cutting mechanic that has a canonical home elsewhere (no delivery/working-dir/session/skills-install restatement present to point at training-architecture.md).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Look-lines name the object and the tell (check_student_facing.md §9, cross-checked against check_pedagogy.md §47's per-phase failure rows).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L9 ("What comes back is a prompt, not a plan. Save it where you will find it.") is a look-line: it sends the student to judge whether the return IS a prompt or a plan, but names no TELL for telling the two apart in the actual text they're looking at. The tell exists, but only in the maintainer block (L15): "check the return opens with an instruction rather than a numbered plan." Mechanical cross-check per the template's own instruction ("ask whether the student could catch that failure themselves in the moment"): YES — "opens with an instruction vs. a numbered list of steps" is a structural distinction the student can apply unaided to their own returned text, right now, with no external help. Per the template, its tell is therefore owed in BODY and its absence is a REVISE. Harm check: L15 itself names plan-instead-of-prompt as the DOMINANT failure at the training's artefact-producing beat ("the student leaves without the one artefact the module exists to produce"); the escape hatch is explicitly written for "trainer or self" use, but sits where a self-checking student never reads it. This is not a proxy match without the harm — it is the file's own documented dominant failure with a self-executable fix one clause away, unused. No maintainer accept-note covers this specific gap: the accept-notes present (L17's §6 carve-out, L19's prompt-block anchoring, L21-22's live-test caveat, L24's cut note) each address a different question, none the missing tell.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Extend L9 with the structural tell already written at L15 — e.g. "What comes back is a prompt, not a plan: it opens with an instruction, not a numbered list of steps." Stays body prose per §16's carve-out for optional refinements and §56's engineer-audience default (self-catchable in under a minute -> body callout, not a new fenced prompt); no time-budget impact, no new registry prompt needed.
